surprises.description: December revenue guidance of $4.8 billion is above the $4.49 billion consensus and within the preview’s $4.7–4.9 billion base case, but below its $4.9–5.1 billion WDC-implied bar. The guide is therefore solid against consensus but short of the more demanding expectation the preview said mattered most.
surprises.fact_evidence: “December quarter guidance calls for revenue of $4.8 billion (plus or minus $100 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “WDC's guide implies the real bar is $4.9–5.1B”; “Base … $4.7–4.9B.”

surprises.description: December EPS guidance of $9.20 exceeds the preview’s key threshold of $9.00 and the $8.38 consensus, although it falls just short of the preview’s bull-case threshold of $9.25. That makes the EPS outlook better than the stated central bar, even as the revenue guide misses the WDC-implied range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “December quarter guidance calls for … non-GAAP EPS of $9.20 (plus or minus $0.20).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS north of $9.00”; “EPS ≥$9.25” in the bull scenario.

surprises.description: September-quarter gross and operating margins came in modestly above the preview’s ranges: gross margin was 57.8% versus 56–57% expected, and operating margin was 50.7% versus 49–50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 510 basis points sequentially to a record 57.8%, while operating margin rose 610 basis points to 50.7%.”

surprises.description: Seagate’s balance sheet outlook is stronger than the preview’s expectation of continued deleveraging: it regained investment-grade status and expects to exit the calendar year net cash positive, rather than merely around the preview’s cited 0.4x net leverage baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Seagate regained investment-grade status, reduced principal debt to approximately $1.6 billion after October repayments, and expects to be net cash positive exiting the calendar year with net leverage of 0.2x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Committed to ~$1.2B of debt retirement in the September quarter”; “Net debt ~0.4x EBITDA.”

surprises.description: The company plans a significant step-up in share repurchases starting in the March quarter, a more concrete and aggressive buyback plan than the preview’s open question about the pace of buybacks after debt repayment. The 3% dividend increase itself was in line with the preview’s expectation of a dividend action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to significantly step up share repurchases starting the March quarter toward its 75% free cash flow return model, with $4.4 billion remaining on authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital returns — FCF … buyback pace post the $1.2B debt retirement, and any dividend action. WDC raised its dividend … a matching move would help.”

surprises.description: Contract coverage remains centered on calendar 2028, rather than broadly extending into 2029 or 2030 as the preview hoped, but some cloud agreements do extend to 2030. This is a partial extension, not the broad horizon change the preview identified as a potential rebuttal to oversupply concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The vast majority of nearline exabyte supply is allocated under long-term agreements through calendar 2028 with some cloud agreements extending to 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “‘Allocated into 2028’ needs to become ‘2029’ or ‘2030’”; “if the language is unchanged, bears will call it a stall.”

surprises.description: The September quarter generated record free cash flow of nearly $1.5 billion, well above the prior quarter’s $1.1 billion level that the preview highlighted while asking about cash generation and capital returns. The preview did not provide a specific Q1 free-cash-flow forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record free cash flow of nearly $1.5 billion, up 32% sequentially and more than tripling year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that external component-cost increases are partly offsetting internal cost declines, a cost headwind, while saying those increases are being passed through via pricing. The preview focused on pricing upside and margin progression but did not anticipate this specific cost-and-pass-through detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher external component costs are partially offsetting internal cost declines but are being passed through via pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pricing per terabyte / price-per-exabyte commentary”; “Any quantification of realized price increases — or evidence that LTAs are being repriced — is the cleanest read on whether the margin story has another leg.”

surprises.description: Seagate demonstrated 8TB per disk in the lab, a technical milestone not anticipated in the preview. The preview discussed the Mozaic 4 ramp but did not mention this higher-density lab demonstration.
